blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it

findings.recommendation: Flatten `import` and name its rules. Skip an empty email with an early `continue` instead of wrapping the whole body in `if !row.email.is_empty()`. Extract the per-seat loop, which is written twice (lines 19-26 and 31-36), into one helper such as `add_new_seats(db, account_id, existing, &row.seats)` that filters `seat.contains('@')` once, behind a named predicate such as `is_email_seat`, with a comment saying why a seat without `@` is dropped silently. Turn `if account.plan != row.plan` into a guard with a comment or a named condition saying why seats are added to an existing account only when its plan changed: a newcomer reading line 18 cannot tell, without the plan, whether it is a rule or a mistake, and would likely read the import as "add the missing seats to every existing account", which it does not do. The doc comment on `import` should also say that rows with an empty email and seats without `@` are skipped.
findings.title: `import` nests six levels deep and hides its two unexplained filters
